content: Hong Kong nursing graduates are facing employment difficulties—is this related to the importation of "foreign labour"? Secretary for Health Prof Lo Chung-mau has spent the past few days refuting this, stressing that local nursing graduates have not had their饭碗 taken away. Ah Miu traces the sequence of events, compiles publicly available information, cross-checks the data cited by Lo, and interviews veteran journalist Yeung Kin-hing to analyse the problems that may arise from the authorities' hardline rebuttal of public concerns. Regarding worries that foreign labour is taking local workers' jobs, Ah Miu interviews economics scholar Lee Siu-por to explore why Hong Kong is still importing foreign labour amid rising unemployment; and invites Federation of Hong Kong and Kowloon Labour Unions general secretary Wu Mei-lin to voice grassroots workers' concerns about the continued importation of foreign labour. Collective Report continues to follow up on the resettlement situation at Wang Fuk Court—Ah Miu compiles the difficulties encountered by residents participating in the "Special Sale Scheme" during their flat purchase process; and former district councillor Yiu Kwan-ho shares his views on the subsequent developments following the resignation of Wong Bik-kiu. The Police National Security Department arrested "Explosion Head" online media operators Tang Ho-wing and Li Ying-tsz on the eve of National Day, alleging they engaged in seditious acts outside Prince Edward station on 31 August this year. Ah Miu compiles the sequence of events for everyone.
